clue.text: A bi-machine's miscast round penny, seemingly double-headed

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the penny, enclosing it
something miscast is cast wrongly, so these letters are recast in a new order

parts.note: the letters of 'A bi-machine's' taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: An odd two-sided coin, apparently struck twice by a faulty minting machine so both faces show a head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miscast' reshuffles the letters of A BI-MACHINE'S into AMHISBAENIC, and 'round' wraps that around the penny's P. An amphisbaena is a fabled serpent with a head at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the amphisbaena, a mythical serpent said to have a head at both ends, so seemingly two-headed.

clue.text: Cocktail party being informal, hostess may be heard telling me to remove this? (6, two words)

indicators.note: may be heard says the answer sounds like a phrase that is spoken

parts.note: a hostess at an informal party would tell a guest to take off his tie, which he would call 'my tie'

explanation.surface: At a relaxed drinks party the hostess invites a guest to loosen up and take something off.
explanation.walkthrough: At an informal party the hostess tells a guest to take off his tie; 'may be heard' says that 'my tie', spoken, gives the cocktail's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A mai tai is a rum-based tropical cocktail with lime, orange curacao and almond syrup.

clue.text: Hand placed over tail and almost all of private parts

indicators.note: placed over, in a down clue, puts the hand word above the rest

parts.note: pud is a dialect and childish word for a hand or paw
an end is a tail, the hind part

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: A rather suggestive picture of a hand resting on a backside and much of the genitals.
explanation.walkthrough: Pud is a dialect word for a hand. 'placed over' stacks it above END in this down answer, and 'almost' trims ALL to AL. The definition is an adjective, hence 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudendal is the adjective from pudenda, the external genitals, so it means relating to the private parts.

clue.text: 'He knows nothing,' I growl, over minimum mark

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, places the earlier parts above the final letter

parts.note: to gnar is to snarl or growl
O, a zero, is the lowest possible mark

explanation.surface: A grumbling teacher scoffs that a pupil is ignorant and snarls over his rock-bottom score.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' stacks I and GNAR on top of O, which is zero as a score.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignaro is an ignoramus, a person with no knowledge, from the Italian for ignorant.

clue.text: Lad by misbehaving gets round judge of top quality impudently

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the following pair
misbehaving means acting out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'Lad by' taken as written
a ref, or referee, judges a game
ace means excellent, of top quality

explanation.surface: A badly behaved boy talks cheekily to a top-notch judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges LAD BY into BADLY, which 'round' splits around the referee and the ace; 'gets' only joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To act barefacedly is to act shamelessly or brazenly, with open cheek.

clue.text: Legal dignitary, short portly person doffing cap

parts.note: a fatty is an informal word for a plump person

explanation.walkthrough: 'doffing cap' takes the first letter off FATTY. 'short' belongs to the definition: the answer is an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Atty is the short written form of attorney, a lawyer acting on another's behalf.

clue.text: Extract from William Empson in retrospective — it has its own syntax!

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the extract is read backwards
an extract is a passage taken from a longer text, here the answer runs inside the poet's name

parts.note: the poet and critic, author of Seven Types of Ambiguity

explanation.surface: A literary quotation from the critic William Empson appears in a career review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract from' finds LIAME running across 'William Empson', and 'in retrospective' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail has its own conventions for addresses and messages, a distinct syntax of addressing and formatting.

clue.text: Failure to claim a right, new burden on reigning monarch?

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the burden above the monarch

parts.note: an onus is a burden or duty
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the reigning monarch when this appeared

explanation.surface: A fresh duty laid on the Queen, perhaps for neglecting a privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down answer 'on' sets the burden above ER, which stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth II, monarch when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: In law nonuser is the neglect to use a right, which can lead to its loss.

clue.text: Fat-cheeked fellow cracking boned meat?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Shakespearean word for a person with fat cheeks
second meaning: the jaws, which crunch through meat on the bone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow cracking' looks like a person inside meat, but the clue gives two senses of one word: an old name for a chubby-cheeked man, and the jaws that chew bony meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chops are the jaws or cheeks, and Shakespeare uses the word for a fat-faced person.

clue.text: Bit of marine life into which smart money may be diverted

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside into another course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'smart money' taken as written

explanation.surface: A sea creature into which shrewd investors might divert their funds.
explanation.walkthrough: Smart money is cash placed by shrewd investors; 'may be diverted' says its letters are shuffled to make the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Asymmetron is a genus of lancelets, small fish-like creatures living in the sea, so a bit of marine life.

clue.text: Roe? Such, I cede, could be nude Erica streaking!

indicators.note: could be says one set of letters may be rearranged into another
streaking suggests a wild dash about, signalling the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters of 'nude Erica' taken as written
the letters of 'I cede', the extra letters inside the fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky exclamation imagining a woman called Erica streaking naked past, with a fishy pun on roe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Such, I cede' as 'this answer plus I, C, E, D, E': 'could be' and 'streaking' say those letters together rearrange to NUDE ERICA. Take ICEDE out and four letters are left.
explanation.definitionFit: Raun is a Scots and dialect word for fish eggs, the spawn or hard roe of a fish.

clue.text: Checked about opening after makeover?

indicators.note: opening says the word for about comes first, at the start

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to invest a town is to besiege it, holding it in check

explanation.surface: Someone examined a shop's grand opening after its refit.
explanation.walkthrough: Invest has an old military sense, to surround and besiege, so a town held in check is invested. 'opening' puts RE in front. Invest also means to clothe, hence the fresh clothes of a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone is to dress them in robes, so one reclothed after a makeover is reinvested, a playful sense.

clue.text: Our grubs are willow feeders smooth Gat hit for six

indicators.note: a cricket phrase for being knocked flying, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'smooth Gat' taken as written

explanation.surface: A boast from creatures whose larvae feed on willow, the wood of cricket bats, beside a gangster's gun struck for six.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the insects themselves. 'hit for six', a big cricket hit over the boundary, scatters the letters of SMOOTH GAT; a gat is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Goat moth caterpillars bore into willow and other trees, so the moths could truly claim their larvae feed on willow.

clue.text: I'm smelling of roses — coming up the same

explanation.definitionFit: Otto, or attar, is the fragrant oil distilled from rose petals, so it smells of roses.

clue.text: Diligent Scots turned match — study inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for study within the turned letters
turned means the word for match is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
a den is a small private room for work, a study

explanation.walkthrough: A cup tie is a match; 'turned' reads it backwards as EIT, and 'inside' places a den, a private study, within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eident is a Scots word meaning industrious or diligent, so the definition carries its regional label.

clue.text: PA having little time to worry

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to annoy is to worry or pester someone

explanation.surface: A personal assistant short of time is left fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is not the assistant but a public address system, and Tannoy is the trade name that became the British word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tannoy is a public-address loudspeaker system, the brand name used generically in Britain.

clue.text: Parrot hiding in a ti tree

indicators.note: a hiding is a thrashing, so these letters get beaten into a new order

parts.note: the letters of 'a ti tree' taken as written

explanation.surface: A parrot is concealed in a ti tree, a palm-like plant of New Zealand and the Pacific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird hiding in the tree, but it is the verb meaning repeat; 'hiding' is the beating that shuffles A TI TREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot something is to repeat it mechanically, and to iterate is to say or do again.

clue.text: Boring creature cut short after wag muttered peevishly

indicators.note: after says the shortened creature follows the wag

parts.note: a wit is a joker, a wag

indicators.note: cut short means its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a teredo is a shipworm, a mollusc that bores into wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' means drilling, not dull: the teredo bores into timber. 'cut short' trims it to TERED, which 'after' sets behind the wag.
explanation.definitionFit: To witter is to chatter or mutter on in a peevish way, so wittered is a past-tense match.

clue.text: Bit of mosaic showing Greek deity group turned up

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
a set is a group

explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small cubes of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Following river is caught in fringes of stream — it's clearly wrong

indicators.note: following says the next part comes after the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

indicators.note: caught in means the little word is held inside the stream's edges
fringes are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters of stream are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of stream

explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, England. 'fringes of' leaves SM from 'stream', 'caught in' makes SISM, and 'Following' puts that after the river rather than meaning F.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsism is a statement that is obviously untrue, the opposite of a truism.

clue.text: Useful thing to have, slotted in to device that's complicated?

definitions.text: Useful thing to have, slotted in to device that's complicated?

complicated letters are tangled, so to device is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of 'to device' taken as written
an asset is something useful or valuable to have

explanation.definitionFit: A videocassette is the tape cartridge loaded into a recorder, a useful item to have for watching or taping programmes.

clue.text: Withdraw from papal seat almost having embraced Anglican church

almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.definitionFit: To secede is to break away formally from a body or alliance.

clue.text: A couple of piggies in the grass

explanation.definitionFit: Toetoe is a tall New Zealand plant of the reed and pampas family, a kind of grass.

clue.text: Descriptive of some fabric that'll make Noele notice?

clue.text: End of foreplay in the heather, this being the positon?

clue.text: Ferns beginning to thrive on a headland

clue.text: Cat discomfited by rat bite (not adult)

clue.text: Approaching piece of fine art, overawed (6, two words)

clue.text: Workout in progress for former policeman

parts.note: PE is physical education, a workout at school
something on is happening, in progress
